1D Gaussian kernel smoothing by FFT, with periodic boundaries

Source: R/kernel-smoothing.R
ker.smooth.fft.Rd

Smooths values z sampled at equally-spaced points x with a Gaussian kernel of standard deviation bandwidth, using an FFT.

Usage

ker.smooth.fft(x, z, bandwidth)

ker.smooth.1D.fft(x, z, bandwidth)

Arguments

x

Numeric vector of equally-spaced grid points.

z

Numeric vector of values at x (same length).

bandwidth

Standard deviation of the Gaussian smoothing kernel.

Value

A numeric vector of length length(z) + 1: the smoothed values at the points halfway between successive x, and half a grid step before the first and after the last. When x are the midpoints of histogram bins, as from hist.weighted(), these are the bin edges.

Not interchangeable with ker.smooth.conv()

This is not simply a faster version of ker.smooth.conv(): the two treat the boundaries differently, and generally return different values.

  • ker.smooth.conv() extends the series by reflection (c(y, rev(y))), which is the right assumption for a curve that is not periodic — such as the temporal triggering kernel, whose lag axis simply stops at the cutoff.

  • ker.smooth.fft() extends the series periodically (c(z, z)), which is the right assumption for a genuinely cyclical curve — such as the day-of-week and month-of-year background components, where the value at Saturday midnight really does wrap round to Sunday.

The package uses each accordingly: temporal_base_weekly() and temporal_base_monthly() call this function, while trigger_reestimate_temporal() calls ker.smooth.conv(), and trigger_reestimate_spatial() calls ker.smooth.2D.fft() (which, despite also being FFT-based, reflects rather than wraps). Substituting one for another "for speed" will silently change the estimates near the boundaries.

References

D'Angelo et al. (2024); see spHawkes-package.

Examples

# Periodic smoothing over a week; the result has one value per break
breaks <- seq(0, 7, by = 0.05)
h <- hist.weighted(c(1, 1, 2, 5, 5, 5), rep(1, 6), breaks = breaks)
smooth <- ker.smooth.fft(h$mids, h$density, bandwidth = 0.5)
plot(breaks, smooth, type = "l", xlab = "Day of week", ylab = "Smoothed density")
